title: GPU Memory Runway Controller — dynamic buffer allocation for weights/KV/activations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight GPU Memory Runway Controller (MRC) that maintains a dynamic 'runway' (buffer) across weights, KV cache, and activations to reduce tail OOMs during continuous batching bursts. The controller should coordinate soft buffer reservations, graded eviction signals, and a short-term prefetch/deferral policy so interactive requests maintain latency SLOs without overprovisioning reserved GPU capacity.
background: We observe intermittent token-latency spikes and rare OOMs under mixed workloads where long-context KV usage and adversarial activation spikes coincide with scheduled continuous-batch flushes. Existing solutions (static soft-headroom, coarse per-tenant caps) either waste GPU capacity or fail to provide graceful degradation. This ticket defines an orchestrator that trades a small, adaptive runway for improved stability and fewer fallbacks to lower-capacity models.
proposal: Design an MRC composed of three components: (1) short-horizon runway estimator that forecasts immediate memory pressure using recent allocation deltas and token-rate signals; (2) runway allocator that assigns ephemeral buffer quotas to active request groups (by priority/route), balancing weight residency, KV retention, and activation headroom; (3) coordinated eviction and deferral controller that issues graded signals to serving pipeline (KV compress, KV partial-evict, reduce batch admission) before hard OOMs. Use conservative ML-informed heuristics for forecasting and allow runtime to fall back to simpler rules if telemetry is noisy.
goals: 1) Reduce customer-facing OOM incidents by 70% for mixed-interactive workloads. 2) Lower average reserved standby GPU headroom by 12% without increasing tail-latency >5% for P0 routes. 3) Provide observable metrics and SLO gating to enable safe rollout.
non_goals: Full multi-tenant re-partitioning of weight memory, long-term training memory optimizations, replacing existing KV eviction algorithms wholesale. The MRC is scoped to online inference serving and short horizon decisions (seconds).
acceptance_criteria: Instrumented runway estimator producing per-pod runway forecasts with <10% median error on internal benchmarks
End-to-end integration test where a 2x synthetic KV spike does not cause OOMs for 95% of runs in lab harness
Telemetry dashboards: runway utilization, emergency-eviction rate, preemptive-deferred-requests, and per-route tail-latency (p99) available in Console
Canary on 5% of non-enterprise workloads shows incident rate reduction and no >5% increase in P99 latency for high-priority routes
Playbook documenting rollback thresholds and mitigations added to runbook repository
risks: Forecasts may be unreliable for highly bursty tenants leading to oscillation; aggressive preemptive eviction could harm quality for KV-heavy responses; added controller complexity increases surface area for bugs in hot codepaths. Mitigations: conservative backoff, safety timeouts, and feature flags to disable per-route runway allocation.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement feature-flagged MRC in staging and run 48h synthetic stress tests; 2) Canary to 5% of traffic (low-risk customers) for 72h with automatic rollback if emergency-eviction > 1/min or p99 latency regresses >5%; 3) Expand to 25% for 1 week while monitoring cost metrics; 4) Full rollout with a phased config push and opt-out controls for enterprise tenants.
test_plan: Unit tests for estimator, allocator, and controller logic; integration tests in the local serving harness with controlled KV and activation pressure; fault-injection tests (simulate telemetry loss, delayed evictions); soak tests under mixed batch patterns for 72h. Add regression scenarios from incident-logs to continuous test matrix.
telemetry_and_alerting: New metrics: mrc_runway_estimate_bytes, mrc_runway_used_bytes, mrc_preemptive_evictions, mrc_partial_kv_evictions, mrc_batch_admission_rate. Alerts: sustained runway_estimate drop < X threshold, emergency_eviction_rate > 0.5/min. Hook existing cost dashboards to measure reserved headroom impact.
implementation_notes: Start with a purely heuristic estimator: exponential moving average of allocation delta + token ingress rate normalized by model footprint. Persist a short trace (3s window) of allocations per-pod to avoid reacting to single-step spikes. The allocator exposes a small API to request runway bytes per request-group; integrate with admission controller to optionally delay low-priority batches by up to 120ms.
migration_plan: MRC starts disabled. Enable estimator-only mode to gather baselines, then enable allocator in flag-protected rollout. Gradually enable eviction signals for low-priority tenants before applying to P0 routes. Ensure configuration per-customer with opt-out via console.
notes: This approach favors minimizing hard OOMs with modest cost savings. If runway proves unreliable in the wild, fallback is to raise soft headroom targets while we iterate on forecasting models. Consider follow-up ticket for ML-based runway predictor if heuristic proves insufficient.
